newsitem.title: THAILAND: Poverty-stricken Thais rally at government house.
newsitem.headline: Poverty-stricken Thais rally at government house.

text.p: Some 3,000 impoverished Thais from the rural northeast have set up camp near Government House and vowed to stay there until the government solves their problems, police said on Saturday.
The well organised throng, members an organisation called the Assembly of the Poor, came to the capital in buses, trains and trucks late on Friday, they told Reuters.
The number of protesters was growing, they said.
"Thousands more are on their way and we expect that at least 10,000 people will be here by later today to voice their demands," a protest leader said.
The protesters vowed not to leave until the government met their demands.
The Assembly of the Poor, led by political activist Banrung Kayota, has staged a series of protests over in recent years.

It is demanding that poor people from northeastern provinces be freed of their debt to the government's Bank of Agriculture and Cooperatives. They also want the government to pay them compensation for building dams on land they claim and give them titles to the claimed land.
Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh met with assembly leaders on Monday in a northern town in a bid to dissuade them from coming to Bangkok. He accepted their demands for consideration.

But, "the government did not set a time frame on settling our problems so we have to come to Bangkok to pressure for the quicker solution," Wanida Thantayapitak, a protest leader, told reporters. reuter sut ram
